title: Canonicalize SparseTensorEntry coordinates without a transient duplicate-axis set
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: SparseTensorEntry coordinate construction already had to canonicalize the bounded coordinate sequence by axis name, but it also built a transient set of every validated axis name solely to detect duplicates before that sort. The extra hash container duplicated information available from the mandatory canonical order and made valid coordinate canonicalization depend on hashing each axis name.
primary_claim: SparseTensorEntry now validates all bounded coordinate pairs, sorts the validated pairs once into the existing canonical order, and rejects duplicate axis names by adjacent comparison after canonicalization. Coordinate hashing is no longer required for constructor duplicate detection, while deterministic ordering and fail-closed duplicate refusal are preserved.
gardener_decision: Use the coordinate tuple's mandatory canonical sort itself for duplicate-axis detection instead of retaining a parallel hash set. Keep the bounded-input guard, validation order, canonical coordinate ordering, and exact fail-closed duplicate error semantics without introducing another lookup abstraction.
acceptance: SparseTensorEntry coordinate canonicalization does not hash every validated axis name into a transient duplicate set
unsorted unique coordinates remain deterministically canonicalized by axis name
duplicate coordinate axis names remain fail-closed after canonicalization
